mainTopic: The liability and the 'owner with him' (בבעלים) exemption of a שואל and a שומר שכר: injury and death, theft and loss, and negligence.
overview: The amud opens by finishing a challenge to רבי נתן, who uses the word 'או' in 'ונשבר או מת' for an extra teaching. The גמרא answers that even רבי יאשיה agrees, because logic alone shows that injury is just a 'partial death.' So 'או' is not needed to divide the two cases. Next the גמרא looks for the source that a שואל pays for גניבה ואבידה. It finds it in a ברייתא's קל וחומר from the שומר שכר, and defends that קל וחומר against a refutation about כפל for an armed bandit. Then it asks why a שואל בבעלים is exempt for theft and loss. After several attempts fail, it answers with the rule of דיו and with the ו׳ of 'וכי ישאל', which links the שואל and שומר שכר sections. Finally, רב אחא and רבינא disagree whether negligence בבעלים is exempt. The disagreement depends on whether a verse reaches back to the שומר חנם section. A proof from our משנה is pushed away, and the גמרא's explanation of the משנה's wording continues on the next amud.

steps.title: End of the quoted source: separate items stand alone unless the verse says 'together'
steps.stepSummary: The last words of רבי יונתן's opinion in the ברייתא, which the גמרא used to suggest that רבי נתן follows only רבי יונתן.
steps.simpleTranslation: …unless the verse spells out for you 'together' (יחדו).
steps.whatsHappening: We are joining at the tail end of a quote. רבי יונתן is saying that when a verse lists two things, each one counts on its own unless the verse explicitly says 'together.'
steps.deeperAnalysis: The גמרא brought this ברייתא to challenge רבי נתן, who uses the word 'או' in 'ונשבר או מת' for an extra teaching. For רבי יאשיה, listed items go together unless the verse divides them, so 'או' would be used up dividing injury from death. Only for רבי יונתן, for whom items stand alone anyway, is 'או' free for רבי נתן's teaching.

keyTerms.meaning: Together; the word that would tell us both items must happen at once
That it spells out / specifies
The verse (the Torah's text)

steps.confusionAlert: This line is not a new opinion starting here. It is the closing words of רבי יונתן's statement, quoted earlier as part of the challenge against רבי נתן.

phrases.english: unless the verse specifies for you "together."

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Completes the ברייתא cited in the preceding challenge (before this section) about רבי יאשיה and רבי יונתן.
steps.kashyaTarget: רבי נתן's use of 'או' in 'ונשבר או מת' for an extra teaching, which seems to need 'או' to be free from its dividing job.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: For רבי יאשיה, items stay joined unless the verse divides them, so 'או' would be needed to divide injury from death and could not be used for anything else. So רבי נתן seems to follow only רבי יונתן.

steps.title: Even רבי יאשיה agrees here, because logic already splits the cases
steps.stepSummary: רבי נתן can fit even רבי יאשיה, since no verse is needed to separate injury from death. Logic says injury is just a partial death.
steps.simpleTranslation: You can even say this follows רבי יאשיה. Here there is no need for a word to divide the cases. Why? It is simple logic: what difference does it make whether the animal was killed completely or killed partly?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers the challenge. It says רבי נתן works even according to רבי יאשיה, because in this case common sense already splits the two cases.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Normally רבי יאשיה would need 'או' to split injury from death. But injury and death are the same kind of loss: the owner does not get back the animal in the condition it was lent. So logic alone (סברא) makes each one enough by itself, 'או' is not needed to divide, and it stays free for רבי נתן's teaching even according to רבי יאשיה.

keyTerms.meaning: You can even say: a way of showing the view fits even the other side
To divide, to make each item count on its own
Logical reasoning, as opposed to a verse
Killed it
Half, partly

steps.whatToRemember: Injury of a borrowed animal is treated as a 'partial death.' Logic alone makes injury and death separate grounds for liability, so רבי נתן fits both רבי יאשיה and רבי יונתן.

phrases.english: You can even say it follows Rabbi Yoshiya,
here there is no need for a word to divide.
phrases.notes: In the borrower's verse, there's no need for 'או' to split injury from death.

phrases.english: What is the reason? It is logical reasoning:
what difference does it make to me if he killed it entirely,
or what difference does it make to me if he killed it halfway.
phrases.notes: 'Killed it halfway' means injured it.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge that רבי נתן follows only רבי יונתן.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Shows the dispute is irrelevant here, because logic, not the verse, separates the cases.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: Under רבי יאשיה, 'או' is needed to split the cases, so it is not free for רבי נתן's teaching. That would mean רבי נתן holds like רבי יונתן.
steps.terutzMaskana: Injury is a partial death, so logic makes each case enough by itself. 'או' is not needed to divide them, so even רבי יאשיה can use it for רבי נתן's teaching.

steps.title: Where do we learn that a borrower pays for theft and loss?
steps.stepSummary: A new question: what is the source that a שואל is liable when the animal is stolen or lost?
steps.simpleTranslation: From where do we know that a borrower is liable for theft and loss?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא starts a new topic. It asks for the source that a borrower must pay if the borrowed item is stolen or lost.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The verse for a שואל openly mentions only 'ונשבר או מת' (injured or died). Theft and loss are not written there, so the גמרא wants to know where that liability comes from.

keyTerms.meaning: Theft
Loss
A borrower (uses an item for free)
From where do we know this?

phrases.english: Theft and loss with a borrower: from where do we know?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Moves from injury and death to a new question about theft and loss.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: The source for a שואל's liability for גניבה ואבידה.

steps.title: A suggested source: learn it from injury and death
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא raises a possible idea: learn theft and loss from injury and death, where the borrower is already known to be liable.
steps.simpleTranslation: And if you would say: let us learn it from 'injured or died'…
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא suggests one possible answer, only so it can test it. This line sets up the rejection in the next step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The idea is that if the borrower pays for injury and death, which happen out of his control, he should also pay for theft and loss. The phrase 'וכי תימא' signals that the גמרא is about to knock this idea down.

keyTerms.meaning: And if you would say: introduces a suggestion that will be rejected
Let us learn (derive)
Injured and died: the cases written in the verse

phrases.english: And if you would say: let us learn it from injured and died,

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Proposes an answer to the question of step 3.
steps.raayaObject: A שואל's liability for גניבה ואבידה.
steps.raayaSupportSource: The verse's liability for שבורה ומתה.

steps.title: Rejected: injury and death cannot be undone, but a stolen or lost animal might be recovered
steps.stepSummary: The comparison fails. Injury and death are final, while with theft or loss the borrower could still search and bring the animal back.
steps.simpleTranslation: What is special about injured and died? There, it is not possible to make an effort and bring the animal back. Can you say the same about theft and loss, where it is possible to make an effort and bring it back?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא rejects the suggestion with a 'מה ל' argument. It points out a difference that makes injury and death a stricter case than theft and loss.
steps.deeperAnalysis: An injured or dead animal can never return to how it was lent, so it makes sense the borrower pays. A stolen or lost animal still exists and might be found. So maybe the borrower should not have to pay. Because of this difference, we cannot learn theft and loss from injury and death. The next step brings a different source.

keyTerms.meaning: What is special about…? Points out a weak spot in a comparison
To make an effort, to go to trouble
And to bring (it back)
Shall you say? (the same rule here)

steps.confusionAlert: The גמרא is not saying a borrower is exempt for theft and loss. It is only saying this particular source does not work, so it must look for another one.

phrases.english: What is special about injured and died?
That it is not possible to make an effort and bring it back,
shall you say the same about theft and loss,
where it is possible to make an effort and bring it back!

steps.triggerLanguage: מָה לִשְׁבוּרָה וּמֵתָה דְּלָא אֶפְשָׁר לְמִיטְרַח וְאֵתוֹיֵי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Rejects the derivation proposed in step 4.
steps.dechiyaRejectionScope: Rejects only learning theft and loss from injury and death. It does not reject the borrower's liability itself.
steps.dechiyaFlawIdentified: Injury and death are permanent and cannot be fixed. Theft and loss might be fixed by finding the animal, so they are a weaker case.

steps.title: A ברייתא learns theft and loss through a קל וחומר from a paid watchman
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא answers the question from step 3 with a ברייתא. A שומר שכר is exempt for injury and death but liable for theft and loss. So a שואל, who is liable for injury and death, should surely be liable for theft and loss.
steps.simpleTranslation: Rather, it is like this ברייתא: 'And it is injured or dies.' From this I only know about injury and death. Where do we learn theft and loss? You can say a קל וחומר: a paid watchman is exempt for injury and death, yet he is liable for theft and loss. A borrower is liable for injury and death, so isn't it logical that he is liable for theft and loss too? And this is a קל וחומר that has no refutation.
steps.whatsHappening: The first idea failed in step 5, so the גמרא brings a new source from a ברייתא. It uses a קל וחומר from the שומר שכר.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Earlier the גמרא tried to compare theft and loss to injury and death, and that did not work. Now it compares the שואל to a different person, the שומר שכר. The שואל is stricter than the שומר שכר in the harder case (injury and death), so he must be at least as strict in the easier case (theft and loss).

keyTerms.meaning: Rather (dropping the earlier idea and bringing a new one)
A logical argument from a lighter case to a stricter case
A paid watchman
Isn't it logical?
There is no refutation against it

steps.whyThisMatters: This is the גמרא's real source for why a שואל pays for theft and loss.

phrases.english: Rather, it is like that which is taught in a ברייתא:
"And it is injured or dies"
phrases.notes: שמות 22:13

phrases.english: I have only an injured or dead animal.
From where do we learn theft and loss?
You can say a קל וחומר:
Now if a paid watchman,
who is exempt for an injured or dead animal,
is still liable for theft and loss,
then a borrower, who is liable for an injured or dead animal,
isn't it logical that he is liable for theft and loss?
And this is a קל וחומר
that has no refutation.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Replaces the source that was rejected in step 5 with a new one.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: The source that a שואל is liable for theft and loss (from step 3).
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: A קל וחומר from a שומר שכר, who is liable for theft and loss even though he is exempt for injury and death.

steps.title: What does 'it has no refutation' mean?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks why the ברייתא added the words 'it has no refutation.'
steps.simpleTranslation: What does 'it has no refutation' mean?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא asks about the extra words at the end of the ברייתא. It is setting up the next step, where it shows which refutation the ברייתא was pushing away.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A ברייתא would not stress 'no refutation' for nothing. It suggests that someone could have raised a refutation, and the ברייתא is saying that refutation does not work. The גמרא wants to know what that refutation was.

keyTerms.meaning: What is? / What does it mean?

phrases.english: What does "it has no refutation" mean?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Asks about the closing words of the ברייתא brought in step 6.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Which possible refutation the ברייתא meant to reject.

steps.title: A possible refutation: the paid watchman pays double for a false armed-bandit claim
steps.stepSummary: Someone might argue that the שומר שכר is stricter in one way. He pays תשלומי כפל if he falsely claims an armed bandit took the animal, and a שואל does not.
steps.simpleTranslation: And if you would say there is room to refute it: what about a paid watchman? He is stricter, because he pays double if he falsely claims that an armed bandit took it.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא states the refutation that someone could raise against the קל וחומר. This is what the ברייתא meant when it said 'no refutation.'
steps.deeperAnalysis: A קל וחומר only works if the שואל is stricter in every way. If the שומר שכר has a stricter rule somewhere, such as paying כפל, then you cannot assume the שואל is always stricter. That would break the argument.

keyTerms.meaning: And if you would say
To refute
Double payment
An armed bandit

phrases.english: And if you would say there is room to refute it:
What about a paid watchman?
He is different, because he pays double
when he makes the claim that an armed bandit took it.
phrases.notes: He means a false claim made with an oath, when it turns out he really had the animal.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Identifies the refutation that step 7 asked about.
steps.kashyaTarget: The קל וחומר from a שומר שכר to a שואל.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The שומר שכר is stricter in one way (כפל for a false armed-bandit claim), so the שואל is not stricter in every way.

steps.title: The borrower is still stricter because he pays the principal outright
steps.stepSummary: Even so, the שואל is stricter. He pays the principal for an armed bandit no matter what, while the שומר שכר pays only if he lies.
steps.simpleTranslation: Even so, the borrower's paying the principal is the stricter rule.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers the refutation. The שואל is still the stricter one.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A שואל cannot free himself even when an armed bandit really did take the animal. He pays the principal. The שומר שכר pays כפל only if he makes a false claim. A rule that always applies is stricter than a fine that comes only from lying, so the קל וחומר stands.

keyTerms.meaning: Even so
The principal (the basic value)
Is greater / stricter

phrases.english: Even so,
the borrower's paying the principal is stricter.
phrases.notes: A borrower pays even if an armed bandit really took it. He has no oath that can free him.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the refutation raised in step 8.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Weighing the two strict rules: the borrower's rule is stricter overall.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The שומר שכר's כפל shows he is sometimes stricter, so the קל וחומר fails.
steps.terutzMaskana: Always paying the principal is stricter than paying כפל only after a lie, so the שואל is stricter and the קל וחומר stands.

steps.title: Second answer: an armed bandit counts as a robber, so there is no double payment
steps.stepSummary: Another answer: the ברייתא holds that an armed bandit is a גזלן, a robber. Since כפל is paid only for a false claim of theft, the שומר שכר does not pay כפל here at all.
steps.simpleTranslation: If you want, say instead: the ברייתא holds that an armed bandit counts as a robber.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא gives a second way to reject the refutation. The refutation itself is based on a mistake.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The first answer agreed that the שומר שכר pays כפל, and said the שואל is still stricter. This answer says the שומר שכר does not pay כפל at all in this case. An armed bandit is a robber, not a thief, and כפל applies only to theft. So there is no stricter rule for the שומר שכר, and the קל וחומר truly has no refutation.

keyTerms.meaning: If you want, say (introduces another answer)
He holds
A robber (takes openly, by force)

steps.whatToRemember: A שואל pays for theft and loss through a קל וחומר from a שומר שכר. The ברייתא calls it a קל וחומר with no refutation: either the שואל is still stricter overall, or an armed bandit is a robber, so the שומר שכר never pays כפל in that case.
steps.confusionAlert: Do not mix up a גנב (thief, who takes in secret) with a גזלן (robber, who takes openly by force). כפל applies only to a claim of theft, so calling the armed bandit a גזלן removes the כפל.

phrases.english: If you want, say instead:
The ברייתא holds that an armed bandit is a robber.
phrases.notes: Double payment applies only to a false claim of theft, not robbery, so there is no double payment here.

steps.triggerLanguage: אִיבָּעֵית אֵימָא קָסָבַר לִסְטִים מְזוּיָּין גַּזְלָן הוּא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: A second answer to the refutation in step 8, alongside the answer in step 9.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Redefining the case: an armed bandit counts as a robber, not a thief.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The שומר שכר pays כפל for a false armed-bandit claim.
steps.terutzMaskana: An armed bandit is a גזלן, and כפל is only for theft, so the שומר שכר has no stricter rule here.

steps.title: We know the borrower pays for theft, but where is his exemption?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא accepts that a שואל pays for theft and loss. It asks for the source that he is exempt for theft and loss when he borrowed the owner along with the animal.
steps.simpleTranslation: We found a source that he is liable. Where do we learn that he is exempt?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא opens a new question. We know a שואל pays for theft and loss, but the תורה only mentions the 'owner with him' exemption for injury and death.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The פסוק 'אם בעליו עמו לא ישלם' is written about a שואל whose animal broke a limb or died. Since theft and loss were only learned through a ברייתא's reasoning, the exemption for them needs its own source.

keyTerms.meaning: We have found (a source)
Liability, having to pay
Exemption, not having to pay
The owner is with him, meaning the owner was working for the borrower at the same time

phrases.english: We have found a source for liability;
for exemption, from where do we know it?
phrases.notes: This is the exemption when the owner was working for the borrower at the time (שמות 22:14).

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Builds on the proof of liability for theft and loss and asks for the matching exemption.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: The source that a שואל בבעלים is exempt for theft and loss.

steps.title: We cannot learn it from injury and death
steps.stepSummary: A suggestion to learn the exemption from injury and death is rejected. Injury and death are unavoidable accidents.
steps.simpleTranslation: And if you say: let us learn it from injury and death. That does not work. Injury and death are different, because they are unavoidable accidents.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא suggests an easy source and then knocks it down right away.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The idea is that if the borrower is exempt for injury and death when the owner is with him, he should be exempt for theft and loss too. But injury and death are אונס, something nobody could prevent. It makes sense to go easy on him there. Theft and loss could have been prevented with careful watching, so the exemption may not carry over.

keyTerms.meaning: And if you would say (brings up a suggestion)
Let us learn (it from)
The animal broke a limb or died
An unavoidable accident
What about X? It is special because... (a standard way to break a comparison)

phrases.english: And if you would say, let us learn it
from a case where it broke a limb or died,
what about breaking a limb or dying?
They are special because they are an unavoidable accident!

steps.triggerLanguage: וְכִי תֵּימָא נֵילַף מִשְּׁבוּרָה וּמֵתָה, מָה לִשְׁבוּרָה וּמֵתָה שֶׁכֵּן אוֹנֶס
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Offers a possible answer to step 11 and rejects it.
steps.dechiyaRejectionScope: Rejects learning the theft/loss exemption from the injury/death exemption.
steps.dechiyaFlawIdentified: Injury and death are אונס, which is a lighter case than theft and loss, which could have been prevented.

steps.title: Learn it from the paid watchman instead
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא suggests learning the borrower's exemption for theft and loss from a שומר שכר.
steps.simpleTranslation: Rather, learn it from a paid watchman.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא gives a new source. A שומר שכר is exempt for theft and loss when the owner was working for him, so the borrower should be exempt too.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Theft and loss are exactly the cases where a שומר שכר pays. If the 'owner with him' exemption covers him there, it covers theft and loss in general, including for a שואל. This avoids the problem of comparing to אונס.

keyTerms.meaning: Rather (brings a new approach)
He learns (one law from another)
A paid watchman

phrases.english: Rather, learn it from a paid watchman.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Replaces the rejected source from step 12.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: The borrower's theft/loss exemption is learned from the שומר שכר's theft/loss exemption.

steps.title: Where does the paid watchman's exemption come from?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks for the source that a שומר שכר is exempt when the owner was working for him.
steps.simpleTranslation: And the paid watchman himself, from where do we know it?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא checks the new source. Where did we learn the paid watchman's exemption in the first place?
steps.deeperAnalysis: The 'owner with him' פסוק is written about a שואל, not a שומר שכר. So the שומר שכר's exemption must also come from somewhere. We need to see whether that source holds up.

keyTerms.meaning: Himself, itself
From where do we know it?

phrases.english: And the paid watchman himself, from where do we know it?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Questions the source proposed in step 13.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: The source for the שומר שכר's exemption when the owner was working for him.

steps.title: The paid watchman learns from the borrower
steps.stepSummary: The שומר שכר's exemption is learned from the שואל. Just as a borrower is exempt when the owner is with him, so is a paid watchman.
steps.simpleTranslation: We learn the paid watchman's liability from the borrower's liability. Just as there, when the owner is with him, he is exempt, so too here, when the owner is with him, he is exempt.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers that the שומר שכר's exemption comes from comparing him to the שואל.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The borrower is exempt in his liable cases (injury and death) when the owner is with him. So the paid watchman should be exempt in his liable cases (theft and loss) when the owner is with him.

keyTerms.meaning: The liability (the cases where he must pay)
Just as there... so too here (a comparison)
With the owner (working for him)

steps.confusionAlert: Watch the circle. The borrower's theft/loss exemption was supposed to come from the paid watchman, but the paid watchman's exemption itself comes from the borrower's injury/death exemption. The next step points out the problem.

phrases.english: We learn the liability of a paid watchman
from the liability of a borrower:
just as there, with the owner, he is exempt,
phrases.notes: 'There' is the borrower, whose פסוק says he is exempt when the owner is with him.

phrases.english: so too here, with the owner, he is exempt.

steps.triggerLanguage: גָּמְרִי חִיּוּבָא דְּשׁוֹמֵר שָׂכָר מֵחִיּוּבָא דְּשׁוֹאֵל
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers step 14.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: The שומר שכר's 'owner with him' exemption is learned by comparing his liability to the שואל's liability.

steps.title: That comparison falls to the same objection
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks how this comparison works. If it is a simple comparison (במה מצינו), it can be broken the same way as before: the borrower's cases are אונס.
steps.simpleTranslation: How is it learned? If it is through 'what do we find,' it can be refuted as we refuted before: those cases are unavoidable accidents!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא challenges the source from step 15 by asking what method of learning it uses. It shows that a simple comparison fails.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The borrower's exemption is written only for injury and death, which are אונס. So comparing to it cannot teach an exemption for the paid watchman's theft and loss. These are preventable, which is the same weakness pointed out in step 12.

keyTerms.meaning: Through what (method)?
'What do we find': learning one case from a similar case
To refute, to break the comparison
As we refuted (earlier)

steps.whatToRemember: A simple comparison (במה מצינו) to the borrower's injury/death exemption can always be pushed away, because injury and death are אונס. The next step finds a source that this objection cannot break.

phrases.english: Through what method is it learned?
If through 'what do we find,'
it can be refuted, just as we refuted before:
phrases.notes: This points back to the objection in step 12.

phrases.english: because those are unavoidable accidents!

steps.triggerLanguage: בְּמַאי גָּמַר? אִי בַּמָּה מָצִינוּ, אִיכָּא לְמִיפְרַךְ כִּדְפָרְכִינַן
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Attacks the source given in step 15 using the objection from step 12.
steps.kashyaTarget: Learning the שומר שכר's exemption from the שואל through a במה מצינו.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The borrower's exemption is written for אונס (injury and death). It cannot be stretched to theft and loss, which are preventable.

steps.title: The letter ו׳ links the paid watchman to the borrower
steps.stepSummary: The שומר שכר's exemption בבעלים is not learned by a simple comparison. It comes from the ו׳ in ״וְכִי יִשְׁאַל״, which joins the borrower's section to the paid watchman's section before it.
steps.simpleTranslation: Rather, the verse says "And if he borrows." The "and" adds onto the first topic, so the upper section (the paid watchman) is learned from the lower section (the borrower).
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא gives a new source for the rule that a שומר שכר is exempt when the owner was working for him. The source is the letter ו׳ in the תורה, not a comparison that can be broken.
steps.deeperAnalysis: In step 16, the comparison was attacked because a borrower's case differs from a paid watchman's. Now the גמרא uses a link built into the פסוק itself: the word "and" ties the two sections together. Because the link comes from the text and not from logic, pointing out a difference between the cases cannot break it.

keyTerms.meaning: The letter ו׳ ("and") adds onto the previous topic
The upper section (here, the שומר שכר section)
The lower section (here, the שואל section)

steps.confusionAlert: The direction here is upper learning from lower. The paid watchman (earlier in the פסוקים) learns the בבעלים exemption from the borrower (later in the פסוקים).

phrases.english: Rather, the verse says: "And if he borrows"
phrases.notes: שמות 22:13

phrases.english: the "and" adds onto the first topic,
phrases.notes: The "first topic" is the paid watchman section that comes just before the borrower.

phrases.english: so let the upper one be learned from the lower one.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the attack in step 16 by replacing a breakable comparison with a link taken from the פסוק itself.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Replaces a logical comparison with a textual link (a הקש from the letter ו׳)
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The שומר שכר's exemption was learned through a simple comparison to the שואל, which could be broken.
steps.terutzMaskana: The ו׳ joins the sections, so the שומר שכר takes the בבעלים rule from the שואל no matter how the two cases differ.

steps.title: The borrower still cannot learn from the paid watchman
steps.stepSummary: Step 17 explained the שומר שכר's exemption. But the borrower's exemption for theft and loss בבעלים, which step 13 tried to learn from a שומר שכר, still fails. The paid watchman is more lenient, since he is exempt for injury and death.
steps.simpleTranslation: But still, the borrower cannot learn from the paid watchman, because the comparison can be broken: a paid watchman is exempt for injury and death, so how can you say the same about a borrower, who is liable for injury and death?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא goes back to the other direction: a borrower learning from a paid watchman. It shows that this comparison still does not work.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The ו׳ only taught that the upper section learns from the lower one, meaning the שומר שכר learns from the שואל. It does not teach the reverse. A plain comparison from a שומר שכר to a שואל breaks down, because a שומר שכר is treated more leniently and a שואל is treated more strictly.

keyTerms.meaning: But still
To break (refute) a comparison
An animal that was injured or died

phrases.english: But still, a borrower cannot learn from a paid watchman,
phrases.notes: This goes back to the suggestion in step 13 about theft and loss.

phrases.english: what about a paid watchman? He is exempt for injury and death,
so how can you say the same about a borrower, who is liable for injury and death!

steps.triggerLanguage: וְאַכַּתִּי שׁוֹאֵל מִשּׁוֹמֵר שָׂכָר לָא גָּמַר
steps.relationToPreviousStep: After the שומר שכר's source is fixed, this step shows that the borrower's source from step 13 is still broken.
steps.kashyaTarget: The step 13 idea that a שואל is exempt for theft and loss בבעלים, learned from a שומר שכר
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: A more lenient case (the שומר שכר, exempt for injury and death) cannot teach a leniency to a stricter case (the שואל, liable for injury and death).

steps.title: דיו: the borrower cannot be stricter than his source
steps.stepSummary: A שואל is only liable for theft and loss because of a קל וחומר from a שומר שכר. By the rule of דיו, the result cannot be stricter than its source. Since a שומר שכר is exempt for theft and loss בבעלים, so is a שואל.
steps.simpleTranslation: Rather, how do we know a borrower is liable for theft and loss? He learns it from a paid watchman. And a law learned by a קל וחומר is only as strict as its source. So just as a paid watchman is exempt for theft and loss when the owner was with him, a borrower is also exempt for theft and loss when the owner was with him.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא finds a new way to exempt the borrower. It looks at where his liability for theft and loss comes from in the first place.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The borrower is not exempted by a comparison that can be broken. Instead, his very liability comes only from the paid watchman, through a קל וחומר. The rule of דיו limits that liability to the same size it has in its source. So wherever the paid watchman is exempt, including בבעלים, the borrower's liability for theft and loss never begins.

keyTerms.term: דַּיּוֹ לַבָּא מִן הַדִּין לִהְיוֹת כַּנִּדּוֹן
keyTerms.meaning: It is enough for a law learned by קל וחומר to be like its source, and no stricter
Theft and loss
With the owner, meaning the owner was working for the watchman at the time
For liability
From where do we know it?

steps.whatToRemember: The שומר שכר learns the בבעלים exemption from the שואל through the ו׳. The שואל is exempt for theft and loss בבעלים because of דיו: his liability for theft and loss only comes from the שומר שכר, so it cannot go further than the source.
steps.whyThisMatters: This shows how דיו can produce a leniency: it sets a limit on a liability that only exists because of a קל וחומר.

phrases.aramaic: אֶלָּא גְּנֵיבָה וַאֲבֵידָה בְּשׁוֹאֵל לְחִיּוּבָא מְנָלַן –
phrases.english: Rather, theft and loss for a borrower, to make him liable, from where do we know it?

phrases.english: so too, with theft and loss for a borrower with the owner, he is also exempt.

steps.triggerLanguage: אֶלָּא גְּנֵיבָה וַאֲבֵידָה בְּשׁוֹאֵל לְחִיּוּבָא מְנָלַן
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the קשיא of step 18 by using the rule of דיו in place of a breakable comparison.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Uses the rule of דיו to limit a liability that comes from a קל וחומר
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The borrower's exemption needed a comparison to the paid watchman, and that comparison breaks.
steps.terutzMaskana: The borrower's liability for theft and loss comes only from the paid watchman, so by דיו it stops where his stops, including בבעלים.

steps.title: What about someone who does not accept דיו?
steps.stepSummary: The answer in step 19 works only for those who accept the rule of דיו. The גמרא asks what someone who rejects דיו would say about the borrower's exemption.
steps.simpleTranslation: This works for the one who holds of דיו. But for the one who does not hold of דיו, what can be said?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא challenges the answer it just gave by pointing out that not everyone accepts דיו. It is setting up the search for another answer.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Some תנאים do not accept the rule of דיו. For them, a קל וחומר can make the borrower stricter than the paid watchman, so the exemption בבעלים would not carry over. The גמרא needs a source for the borrower's exemption that works for everyone.

keyTerms.meaning: This works well
For the one who holds of it
For the one who does not hold of it
What can be said?

phrases.english: This works well for the one who holds of "it is enough,"
but for the one who does not hold of "it is enough,"
what can be said?

steps.triggerLanguage: הָנִיחָא לְמַאן דְּאִית לֵיהּ דַּיּוֹ, אֶלָּא לְמַאן דְּלֵית לֵיהּ דַּיּוֹ מַאי אִיכָּא לְמֵימַר
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Limits the answer of step 19 to those who accept דיו, and asks for a source that works for everyone.
steps.kashyaTarget: The דיו-based source for the borrower's exemption in step 19
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The answer depends on a rule that some reject, so it cannot be the source for everyone.

steps.title: The ו׳ links the two sections in both directions
steps.stepSummary: Even without the rule of דיו, the borrower's exemption בבעלים for theft and loss is learned from the ו׳ in ״וְכִי יִשְׁאַל״. It joins the two sections so each one learns from the other.
steps.simpleTranslation: Rather, the verse says "And if he borrows." The letter ו׳ adds onto the first topic. So the upper section learns from the lower one, and the lower section learns from the upper one.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers the question from step 20 for someone who does not accept דיו. The ו׳ ties the שואל section and the שומר שכר section together, and the link works in both directions.
steps.deeperAnalysis: In step 17 the ו׳ was used to bring the exemption בבעלים up from the borrower to the שומר שכר. Now the גמרא says the link also works downward: the שומר שכר section teaches the borrower. So a שואל is exempt for theft and loss בבעלים without needing the rule of דיו.

keyTerms.meaning: The letter ו׳ ("and") adds onto the topic before it
The upper section: the שומר שכר section, which comes first
The lower section: the שואל section, which comes after

steps.whatToRemember: The ו׳ of ״וְכִי יִשְׁאַל״ makes the שומר שכר and שואל sections one unit. Rules move both ways between them.

phrases.english: Rather, the verse says: "And if he borrows,"

phrases.notes: "Upper" is the שומר שכר section and "lower" is the borrower's section right after it.

steps.terutzResolutionType: Textual source: a two-way link made by the ו׳
steps.terutzHavaAmina: Without דיו, the borrower might seem to have no source for being exempt for theft and loss בבעלים
steps.terutzMaskana: The ו׳ joins the sections both ways, so the שואל learns the exemption from the שומר שכר section

steps.title: רב אחא and רבינא disagree about negligence with the owner present
steps.stepSummary: A new topic opens: is a borrower who was negligent בבעלים liable? One אמורא says liable, the other says exempt.
steps.simpleTranslation: It was stated: negligence with the owner present. רב אחא and רבינא disagree about it. One says he is liable, and one says he is exempt.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a new disagreement between אמוראים. The question is a borrower who was negligent while the owner was working for him (פשיעה בבעלים).
steps.deeperAnalysis: Until now the discussion covered אונס, theft and loss בבעלים. Now it asks about negligence, which is a more serious failure. The disagreement depends on whether the exemption בבעלים reaches far enough to cover negligence too.

keyTerms.meaning: Negligence: the watchman did not guard properly
With the owner working for the watchman at the time of the borrowing or guarding

steps.mimraCoreRuling: There is a disagreement over whether a negligent borrower is liable בבעלים: one says liable, one says exempt

steps.title: The liable view: a verse links only to the section right before it
steps.stepSummary: The one who says liable holds that a verse is read together with the section right before it, but not with the section two places back.
steps.simpleTranslation: The one who says he is liable holds that a verse is expounded with the section before it, but not with the section before that one.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא starts explaining the reasoning of the one who says liable. This step sets up the rule that the next step will apply.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Step 21 said the ו׳ links the borrower's section to the שומר שכר section right before it. This view adds a limit: the link stops there and does not reach back to the שומר חנם section, which comes even earlier.

keyTerms.meaning: He holds (this is his reasoning)
A verse is expounded together with the passage right before it
The passage before the one before it, two sections back

phrases.english: The one who says he is liable holds:
a verse is expounded with the section before it,
phrases.notes: "Before it" means the שומר שכר section, right before the borrower's section.

phrases.english: but not with the section before that one,
phrases.notes: That is the שומר חנם section, two places back.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Starts explaining the view in step 22 that says liable
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The borrower's verse links to the section right before it, the שומר שכר, but not to the שומר חנם section

steps.title: Liability for negligence comes only from a קל וחומר
steps.stepSummary: The exemption בבעלים is not written about a שומר חנם, and negligence is not written about a שומר שכר or a שואל. So their liability for negligence comes only through a קל וחומר from the שומר חנם.
steps.simpleTranslation: Therefore "if its owner is with him" is not written about an unpaid watchman. Negligence is also not written about a paid watchman or a borrower. Therefore, the liability of a paid watchman and a borrower comes through a קל וחומר from an unpaid watchman.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא applies the rule from step 23 and works out two results. This sets up how the liable view will reach its answer.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Since the link does not reach the שומר חנם, he has no exemption בבעלים. Negligence liability is written only in the שומר חנם section. So the שומר שכר and שואל are liable for negligence only by a קל וחומר: if even an unpaid watchman pays for negligence, surely a paid watchman and a borrower do. The next step uses this to explain why the exemption בבעלים does not reach their negligence.

keyTerms.meaning: Therefore
"If its owner is with him": the verse that gives the exemption בבעלים
An unpaid watchman
It is not written (it does not apply to that case)

steps.confusionAlert: Do not mix up the two ways a rule is learned. The exemption בבעלים comes from the verse through the ו׳. The liability for negligence comes from a קל וחומר from the שומר חנם. The liable view builds on this difference.
steps.whyThisMatters: This explains why one אמורא makes a negligent borrower pay even בבעלים. His liability comes from a source that never had the exemption בבעלים.

steps.triggerLanguage: הִלְכָּךְ ״אִם בְּעָלָיו עִמּוֹ״ אַשּׁוֹמֵר חִנָּם לָא כְּתִיב
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Applies step 23's rule to show where negligence liability comes from
steps.mimraCoreRuling: A שומר שכר and a שואל are liable for negligence only through a קל וחומר from the שומר חנם, who has no exemption בבעלים

steps.title: Why the owner-exemption does not cover negligence
steps.stepSummary: The 'liable' view explains that the exemption בבעלים applies only to the liabilities written openly for the שואל and the שומר שכר. It does not apply to their negligence liability, which comes only from a קל וחומר.
steps.simpleTranslation: But we cannot say that a שומר שכר and a שואל are also exempt בבעלים for negligence. Why? When the תורה writes "If its owner is with him, he shall not pay" about the borrower and the paid watchman, it is talking only about the liabilities written openly about them.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא finishes the reasoning of the one who says a negligent borrower is liable even בבעלים.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Negligence liability for the שומר שכר and the שואל is never written in the פסוקים; it comes from a קל וחומר from the שומר חנם. The exemption of 'owner with him' sits on the liabilities that are written openly for them, like theft and loss for the שומר שכר, and death and breaking for the שואל. So the exemption never reaches the negligence liability.

keyTerms.meaning: openly, written out clearly in the פסוק
liabilities, things he must pay for
to exempt, to free from paying

steps.whyThisMatters: This shows a key principle: a law that comes only from a קל וחומר is not automatically covered by an exemption written about the explicit laws.

phrases.english: But regarding the exemption of 'with its owner'
phrases.notes: He means: the קל וחומר brings the negligence liability, but it doesn't also bring the owner-exemption along with it.

phrases.english: When it is written, "If its owner is with him, he shall not pay,"
phrases.notes: שמות 22:14

steps.triggerLanguage: אֲבָל בִּבְעָלִים לִפְטוּר אַף בְּשׁוֹמֵר שָׂכָר וּבְשׁוֹאֵל – לָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Completes the 'liable' view's reasoning begun in step 24.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The exemption בבעלים covers only liabilities written openly for the שואל and the שומר שכר, not negligence, which is learned by קל וחומר.

steps.title: Why the other view says he is exempt
steps.stepSummary: The 'exempt' view holds that a פסוק is read with the section before it and also the section two places back. So the owner-exemption reaches the שומר חנם too, and that covers negligence.
steps.simpleTranslation: The one who says exempt holds that a verse is learned together with the section right before it and the section before that. So when it is written "If its owner is with him," it is written about the unpaid watchman too.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא now explains the reasoning of the one who says a negligent borrower is exempt בבעלים.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The section of the שואל comes after the שומר שכר section, which comes after the שומר חנם section. If the פסוק reaches back two sections, the exemption בבעלים applies to the שומר חנם, whose only liability is negligence. So the exemption covers negligence itself, and the borrower who was negligent is exempt too.

keyTerms.meaning: a verse is learned together with the section right before it
and with the section before that one, two places back
unpaid watchman, liable only for negligence

steps.whyThisMatters: The whole argument depends on how far back a פסוק can reach. That is the root difference between the two views.

phrases.english: The one who says exempt holds:
a verse is learned with the section before it
and with the section before that one,

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives the opposing view's reasoning, the mirror image of step 23.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Since the פסוק reaches the שומר חנם, the exemption בבעלים covers negligence, so a negligent borrower בבעלים is exempt.
steps.triggerLanguage: מַאן דְּאָמַר פָּטוּר, קָסָבַר: מִקְרָא נִדְרָשׁ לְפָנָיו וְלִפְנֵי פָנָיו

steps.title: A proof from the משנה, which mentions only a borrower
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא brings our משנה, which teaches the owner-exemption only for a borrower and does not mention a שומר חנם. This seems to show that the exemption does not cover negligence.
steps.simpleTranslation: We learned: one who borrowed a cow and borrowed its owner with it, or borrowed the cow and hired its owner with it, or borrowed or hired the owner first and afterward borrowed the cow, and it died: he is exempt. But it does not teach a case of an unpaid watchman!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא tries to prove the 'liable' view from the wording of our משנה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A שומר חנם is liable only for negligence. If the owner-exemption covered negligence, the משנה should have taught that a שומר חנם בבעלים is exempt too. Since it is left out, it seems the exemption does not cover negligence.

keyTerms.meaning: hired, paid someone for work
it does not teach, the משנה leaves it out

phrases.english: We learned:
One who borrows a cow and borrowed its owner with it,
one who borrows a cow and hired its owner with it,
or borrowed its owner or hired him
and afterward borrowed the cow,
and it died: he is exempt.
Whereas an unpaid watchman, it does not teach!
phrases.notes: This is the proof: a שומר חנם only pays for negligence, so leaving him out suggests negligence isn't covered.

steps.triggerLanguage: תְּנַן: הַשּׁוֹאֵל הַפָּרָה וְשָׁאַל בְּעָלֶיהָ עִמָּהּ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Tests the two views against the משנה, seeming to support the 'liable' view.
steps.raayaObject: The view that a negligent borrower בבעלים is liable.
steps.raayaSupportSource: The משנה teaches the owner-exemption only for a borrower and leaves out the שומר חנם.

steps.title: The משנה leaves out the paid watchman too
steps.stepSummary: The proof is pushed away: the משנה does not mention a שומר שכר either, even though he is surely exempt בבעלים for theft and loss. So leaving someone out proves nothing.
steps.simpleTranslation: And by your reasoning, does it teach a paid watchman?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא rejects the proof from the משנה by turning the same question back on it.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Everyone agrees a שומר שכר is exempt בבעלים for theft and loss, as the גמרא showed from the ו׳ of 'וכי ישאל'. Yet the משנה does not mention him. So the משנה simply speaks about a borrower and is not listing every watchman, and the missing שומר חנם shows nothing.

keyTerms.meaning: and by your own reasoning
does it teach?

steps.whatToRemember: The proof from the משנה fails, since the משנה also leaves out the שומר שכר. The גמרא's explanation of the משנה's wording continues on the next amud.

phrases.english: And by your reasoning:
does it teach a paid watchman?
phrases.notes: A שומר שכר is surely exempt בבעלים for theft and loss, yet the משנה still doesn't mention him.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Rejects the proof brought in step 27.
steps.dechiyaRejectionScope: The whole proof from the משנה's silence about the שומר חנם.
steps.dechiyaFlawIdentified: The משנה also leaves out the שומר שכר, who is certainly exempt בבעלים, so leaving out a case does not prove the law does not apply to it.

steps.title: Starting to explain the תנא's choice
steps.stepSummary: With the word אלא, the גמרא starts a new explanation of why the משנה names only the borrower: the תנא chose to teach a certain kind of matter.
steps.simpleTranslation: Rather, the תנא taught the matter…
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא is setting up its next move. It begins to explain why the משנה mentions only the borrower, and the sentence is finished on the next amud.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Step 28 showed that leaving someone out of the משנה proves nothing, since the שומר שכר is also left out. Now the גמרא gives a positive reason for the תנא's choice. It introduces the idea that he picked a particular kind of 'matter' to teach, and the next words will say which kind.

keyTerms.meaning: Rather. It introduces a new explanation instead of the earlier one.
The teacher of the משנה, the one who chose its wording.
A matter or thing, here a point of law the תנא chose to teach.

steps.confusionAlert: This sentence is not finished here. Don't try to understand the full reason yet; just know that the גמרא is starting to explain why the משנה chose to mention only the borrower.

phrases.english: Rather, the tanna [taught] the matter
phrases.notes: The sentence keeps going on the next amud, where the גמרא says which kind of matter the תנא chose to teach.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: After Step 28 showed that the משנה's silence proves nothing, this step begins to give a positive reason for why the תנא mentions only the borrower.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Explains the משנה's choice of wording (still being set up here)
steps.terutzHavaAmina: Mentioning only the borrower might seem to show that the owner-exemption does not cover the שומר חנם's negligence.
steps.terutzMaskana: The תנא picked a certain kind of matter to teach. The full reason comes in the continuation.
